**Summary of analysis:**

**Test image features:**
- Tomato stem/branch with an elongated, longitudinal brown canker running along the stem surface
- Lighter tan/cream margins bordering the darker brown necrotic center
- Stem is otherwise green and turgid (not collapsed)
- No white mycelium visible
- Lesion near a node junction

**Evidence against other classes:**
- Sclerotinia/Gray Mold: no white mycelium
- Southern Blight: no soil-line location or sclerotia
- Phytophthora Blight: stem would be more water-soaked/collapsed
- Anthracnose: shows circular fruit lesions
- Verticillium Wilt/Bacterial Wilt: shows leaf wilting symptoms, not external stem canker
- All leaf-focused diseases (Early Blight, Late Blight, Septoria, etc.): wrong plant part

**Best match:** The elongated, longitudinal tan-to-brown canker stripe on the tomato stem with lighter borders is the hallmark symptom of **Bacterial Canker and Wilt of Tomato** (*Clavibacter michiganensis* subsp. *michiganensis*). This pathogen characteristically causes superficial longitudinal streaking and canker formation on stems, exactly matching the test image.
